R-POWER.title: Perseverance Landing Press Kit: Power
R-POWER.fact: About 110 W at mission start; two batteries about 43 Ah each; generation and storage are distinct.
R-POWER.limit: No usable battery Wh is inferred without voltage, SOC, age, temperature and reserve specifications; reference power is not credited to this proposal.

R-MOBILITY.title: Perseverance Rover Components
R-MOBILITY.fact: About 152 m/h maximum on flat hard ground.
R-MOBILITY.limit: Not a guaranteed mean rate over a science campaign or the selected patches. The proposed model speed is unchanged.

R-DRIVE.title: NASA's Perseverance Breaks Own Rover Driving Record
R-DRIVE.fact: 411.7 m during approximately 4 hours 24 minutes in one documented drive.
R-DRIVE.limit: A historical performance example, not a daily nominal distance or a speed calibration for this model.

SOL.title: NASA GISS Mars24 Technical Notes
SOL.locator: Mean solar day and time conventions
SOL.fact: Mean sol is 24 h 39 min 35.244 s, or 88775.244 s.
SOL.limit: A calendar unit does not imply continuous driving, an operating window or available energy.

H-EVA.title: Apollo 17: Mission Details
H-EVA.fact: Historical lunar EVAs included durations about 7 h 12 min and 7 h 37 min.
H-EVA.limit: Context only, not a Mars EVA duration, suit approval or evidence that this experiment should use seven hours.

H-WORK.title: D-RATS geological field protocols, LPSC 2011 abstract 1334
H-WORK.locator: Field protocol and time/task management, pp.1-2
H-WORK.fact: Approximately ten minutes per documented sample in the reported terrestrial analogue experience.
H-WORK.limit: Not measured Mars task timing. The 420 s light/180 s heavy split is our pending allocation; complete documentation is inside the 600 s, not added twice.

H-METABOLIC.title: NASA/TM-2010-216138
H-METABOLIC.fact: Existing lunar-analogue power anchors for walking, light work and heavy stationary work.
H-METABOLIC.limit: Existing proposed transfer to Mars is retained without coefficient approval; metabolic Wh is not battery energy.

H-OXYGEN.title: NASA BVAD revision 2
H-OXYGEN.fact: Existing model derives oxygen proportionality from 295 W and 0.086 kg/h reference values.
H-OXYGEN.limit: Equivalent dry-gas metabolic demand only; not tank volume, suit capacity, leakage, cooling or CO2-removal validation.

D-NOMINAL.title: Ingenuity Landing Press Kit: Spacecraft
D-NOMINAL.fact: Original test concept included up-to-90-second flights, about 350 W flight power and solar-recharged batteries.
D-NOMINAL.limit: Nominal test envelope, not a universal endurance limit or a guarantee of recharge between our sorties.

D-FLIGHT.title: NASA Ingenuity Helicopter Flight Log
D-FLIGHT.fact: Flight 12 lasted 169.5 s and covered approximately 450 m.
D-FLIGHT.limit: Historical observation, not a certified bound. Compare airborne time, not ground-inclusive elapsed time.

D-BATTERY.title: Battery System Design, Testing and Operation for Perseverance and Ingenuity
D-BATTERY.fact: Beginning-of-life energy estimates include 44.4 Wh at 25 C and 38.8 Wh at 0 C.
D-BATTERY.limit: Temperature-specific reference energy, not guaranteed usable flight energy; thermal and other loads share it.

D-CHARGE.title: When Should Ingenuity Fly?
D-CHARGE.locator: Heating, state of charge and time-of-day discussion
D-CHARGE.fact: Nighttime depletion and morning warming/charging constrain the flight window.
D-CHARGE.limit: No constant recharge time or guaranteed solar supply is derived.

D-WINTER.title: Ingenuity Adapts for Mars Winter Operations
D-WINTER.fact: Season, dust and cold can make overnight demand exceed the energy budget.
D-WINTER.limit: The current 5 W ground wait is not a calibrated overnight survival mode.

D-THERMAL.title: Ingenuity's Final Flight: Lessons Learned
D-THERMAL.locator: Project manager discussion of nighttime energy
D-THERMAL.fact: Operational account identifies overnight heating as a dominant energy use.
D-THERMAL.limit: Not a transferable constant fraction for this model.

R-SOLAR.title: NASA Mars Rover Team's Tilted Winter Strategy Works
R-SOLAR.locator: Opportunity winter energy and dust discussion
R-SOLAR.fact: Solar supply depends on orientation, season and dust; wind effects are variable.
R-SOLAR.limit: A solar architecture would need its own model. Wind cleaning is never a guaranteed recharge event.

source_use_policy: Observed hardware/mission facts constrain interpretation. Distances, station counts, waiting allowances, reserve fraction and allocation rounding in the companion proposal are engineering assumptions, not NASA operational prescriptions.
